idiom_name: Ktor HttpRequestRetry + a stable Idempotency-Key on the request
implementation_notes: Ktor's client plugin does the replay: install(HttpRequestRetry) with retryOnServerErrors(n), exponentialDelay() and optional retryIf/retryOnExceptionIf predicates, plus modifyRequest for per-attempt adjustments. The plugin's defaults retry regardless of HTTP method, so a keyed POST stays the caller's responsibility: bind java.util.UUID.randomUUID() (or a business id) to the logical operation before the call and set it in the request headers, never in modifyRequest. Because cancellation and HttpTimeout interact with retries, the idempotent contract is what makes a cancelled-then-repeated request harmless.
pitfalls: HttpRequestRetry replays any method matching the predicate, so retryOnServerErrors on an unkeyed POST duplicates the write; narrow it with retryIf { request, _ -> request.method in setOf(HttpMethod.Get, HttpMethod.Put, HttpMethod.Delete) } when the endpoint is not keyed.
modifyRequest and every interceptor run before each attempt, so generating the idempotency key there produces one key per retry.
Plugin order matters: HttpRequestRetry should be installed before HttpTimeout, otherwise timed-out attempts surface as failures with an unknown outcome instead of being replayed.
